name: Clifford+T inverse rule (IV′)
summary: A Z- and X-spider joined by three wires (the scalar 1/√2), next to a π/4 Z-state, a π X-spider and a −π/4 Z-effect in a row (the scalar √2), is the empty diagram.
description:
A phase-free Z-spider and X-spider connected by three wires represent the scalar $\frac1{\sqrt2}$. The chain of a Z-spider with phase $\frac\pi4$, an X-spider with phase $\pi$ and a Z-spider with phase $-\frac\pi4$ is $\langle 0| + e^{-i\pi/4}\langle 1|$ applied to $X(|0\rangle + e^{i\pi/4}|1\rangle)$, which is $e^{i\pi/4}+e^{-i\pi/4} = \sqrt2$. So the two components together are the empty diagram.

Ng and Wang use this rule in their complete axiomatisation of the Clifford+T ZX-calculus (with the triangle and $\lambda$-box as extra generators), in place of the inverse rule (IV) of their universal axiomatisation, which uses a $\lambda$-box with label $1-\frac1{\sqrt2}$ and therefore lies outside the Clifford+T fragment. It plays the same role as the [inverse rule](../inverse-rule/) and the [Clifford+T scalar rule (E)](../clifford-t-scalar/): it lets one invert the scalar $\sqrt2$.
notes: The right-hand side is the empty diagram.
